observations: Line 2 uses a late-binding closure: `lambda: i` captures the variable `i`, not its per-iteration value, so all three lambdas share the final value of `i`.
The behavior contract states each callback returns the index captured at creation, but the source does not bind `i` per iteration (e.g., no default-argument `lambda i=i: i`).
Probe p1 `[fn() for fn in callbacks()]` is predicted to return `[2, 2, 2]` rather than the contract-implied `[0, 1, 2]`.
A normal comparison input would be `[lambda i=i: i for i in range(3)]`, predicted to return `[0, 1, 2]`, matching the contract.
No static findings are supplied, so the late-binding defect is only observable via the probe call.
